problem:
| $x$ | $-1$ | $3$ | $7$ | $11$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $4$ | $2$ | $k$ | $6$ |

The table above gives the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ on the closed interval $[-1,11]$ with a regular step size. If the right Riemann sum approximation to the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ with $3$ subintervals defined by the given points has a value of $96$, then what must be the value of $k?$ 

$k=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the graph can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(3)+f(7)+f(11)}})\cdot {{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $3$ | $7$ | $11$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $2$ | $k$ | $6$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(2+k+6)\cdot 4 \\  & =(k+8)\cdot 4 \\  & =4k+32\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are given that $A$ must be  $96,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4k+32 & =96 \\ 4k & =96-32 \\ k & =\frac{64}{4} \\ k & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
